title: feat: Google Sheets offline via XLSX export/import (Option A)
description:
Summary (Option A)

Goal: Add a Google Sheets integration that supports 'local work mode' by exporting a Google Sheet to a local XLSX snapshot, editing it with Ebenezer's existing XLSX pipeline (excelize), and then publishing the result back to Google Sheets.

Key behavior:
- Open a Google Sheet (URL or spreadsheetId) and export to a local XLSX snapshot for offline editing.
- Persist provenance metadata (spreadsheetId, export time, remote modifiedTime/version/etag) alongside the snapshot.
- On publish, re-check remote modifiedTime/version/etag; if changed, display a loud warning and require --force (no merge in v1).
- Publish path focuses on creating a NEW Google Sheet from the edited XLSX (Drive upload + convert), yielding a full clone/edited clone destination.

Implementation needs:
- Google OAuth2 auth flow for CLI + token storage/refresh.
- Drive API: export Google Sheet -> XLSX; upload XLSX with conversion to Google Sheet; read file metadata for mutation warning.
- CLI/UX: commands like gsheets export/open and gsheets publish/sync --new, plus status.

Out of scope v1:
- True conflict mitigation/merging.
- Guaranteed lossless round-trip for every Sheets-only feature; rely on Google Sheets<->XLSX conversion behavior.
close_reason: Duplicate; tracked as task ebenezer-z4m

title: Ctrl+Left not jumping to next filled cell in manual test
description:
Manual test result: Ctrl+Arrow keys do not trigger Excel-style span jump.

Expected (per ebenezer-9hy):
- Ctrl+Arrow should jump to next non-empty cell / edge of filled run in the pressed direction.

Actual (manual test):
- Ctrl+Right does not move at all.
- In fact, any Arrow key with Ctrl (Ctrl+Left/Right/Up/Down) does not move at all.

Environment (reported so far):
- Terminal: Windows Terminal
- Running: WSL2
- Distro: Alpine Linux ("lith" per user)

Repro:
1) Open any sheet in keyboard mode.
2) Press Ctrl+Right (or any Ctrl+Arrow).

Suspect:
- Terminal is sending a different escape sequence than the parser handles, or the environment (tmux/screen/terminal) is swallowing it.

Manual diagnostics request (please collect and paste into this issue):
1) Environment
   - Windows version
   - Windows Terminal version
   - WSL distro version (Alpine release) + whether via ssh
   - Are you inside tmux/screen?
2) What the app does
   - Does Ctrl+Arrow do nothing, move 1 cell, or print characters?
3) Capture escape sequences
   - Run `cat -v` in a shell, press Ctrl+Left/Ctrl+Right/Ctrl+Up/Ctrl+Down, and paste the output.
   - If `cat -v` shows nothing, try in the same terminal: `python -c "import sys,tty,termios; fd=sys.stdin.fileno(); old=termios.tcgetattr(fd); tty.setraw(fd); print(\"press keys, Ctrl-C to stop\");\ntry:\n  while True:\n    b=sys.stdin.buffer.read(1)\n    print(b.hex(), flush=True)\nexcept KeyboardInterrupt:\n  pass\nfinally:\n  termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)"` and press Ctrl+Arrows.
4) Quick workaround check
   - Test outside tmux/screen (if applicable) and note whether it starts working.
close_reason: Resolved: handle additional Ctrl+Arrow escape variants and add automated movement tests
